page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors operating at 3.3 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated physical cores with a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping, eliminating multi-threading resource contention. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 64.0 GB, providing a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation characteristic of compute-focused platforms. Hardware cryptographic support includes hardware-accelerated AES. The instance does not include bundled local storage or discrete graphics accelerators, and it features a 17 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in compute-bound and memory-bound tasks. Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations show upper-decile scoring, reflected in a Clang software compilation score of 63901.0 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 25987.0. Data compression throughput is equally high, delivering 36.46 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression and 457.39 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory subsystem benchmarks show top-tier PassMark memory and database metrics, enabling static web serving throughput of 92.57 GB/sec and Redis write throughput exceeding 93 million operations per second.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires external network-attached volumes for persistent data, which balances against the 17 Gbps network pipe. However, dedicating full physical execution pipelines to each vCPU avoids performance degradation during sustained compute spikes. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio avoids excessive memory spend on processing-heavy pipelines. These architectural traits make c9g.8xlarge an effective option for software build farms, CI/CD runners, distributed batch processing clusters, web application layers, and containerized microservice deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based server featuring 32 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 64.0 GB of memory at a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core) alongside a 17 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU hardware. Performance metrics show top-tier execution across single-core and multi-core Geekbench suites, Clang compilation, and static web serving throughput reaching 92.57 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation reveals upper-decile database operation scores and rapid compression capabilities, backed by 48 MB of L3 cache and strong stress-ng multi-core stability. With consistent dedicated core execution and high computational density, c9g.8xlarge fits compute-bound applications, including continuous integration build nodes, containerized service hosting, parallel batch calculations, and high-traffic web tiers.
